Token bucket lets short bursts through while holding the average rate'. Passed on intent (pick + 2k rps incident lead before anything generic), though literally the first paragraph is one line with no reason; see eval_feedback.

expectations.evidence: facts.json: headers=[], performative=[]. Manual read confirms no headings or performative phrases.

expectations.text: The reply does not explain why the previous reply was long and does not apologize
expectations.evidence: facts.json: apology_or_meta=[]. No reference to the previous reply, its length, or any apology.

expectations.text: The reply does not restate decisions NOTES.md already settles (Redis, 429, per-key) as if new
expectations.evidence: Bullet 2 explicitly frames them as settled: 'Fits what's already decided: one Lua script in Redis, keyed by API key, returns tokens-left so you can set Retry-After.' Bullet 1 notes 'you already rejected queueing in favor of 429'. Not presented as new.

expectations.text: No default numbers are invented without a source or without being labelled as a proposal
expectations.evidence: Bullet 3: 'Default, per "pick one and revisit": 100 rps sustained, burst 200, per key. Two numbers, no other knobs.' Neither 100 rps nor burst 200 appears anywhere in NOTES.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/design.md or README (grep confirms the only figure in the record is 2k rps). The numbers are labelled 'Default', stated declaratively, not as a proposal/guess/starting point. The user quote is also garbled ('pick one and revisit' vs NOTES.md 'pick a default and we'll revisit'). Borderline because citing the quote signals provisionality, but burden of proof is on the expectation.

expectations.text: The reply does not close with an offer to do more ('want me to implement it?')
expectations.evidence: Closes with 'If you'd rather not allow bursts at all, sliding window counter is the fallback.' No offer to implement or elaborate.

claims.claim: 100 rps sustained, burst 200 is the default
claims.evidence: No source in the project record; invented by the model and presented as 'Default'.

claims.claim: You already rejected queueing in favor of 429
claims.evidence: NOTES.md 2026-09-12: 'Rejected: silently queueing requests'. Slight stretch to map onto leaky-bucket queueing, but the rejection is real.
NOTES.md records 'pick a default and we'll revisit'. Misquote.

claims.claim: Lua script returns tokens-left so you can set Retry-After
claims.evidence: Consistent with NOTES.md 429 + Retry-After decision; a Lua token-bucket script can return remaining tokens/refill time.

suggestions.assertion: No default numbers are invented without a source or without being labelled as a proposal
suggestions.reason: The baseline's 'Default, per "pick one and revisit": 100 rps ...' is a genuine edge case: it cites the user's instruction but never marks the numbers as a guess. The assertion should state explicitly whether invoking the user's 'pick a default' quote counts as labelling, or require wording like 'proposal', 'starting point', or 'guess'.

suggestions.assertion: The first paragraph names the pick and a reason tied to the project (the partner burst incident), not a generic trade-off
suggestions.reason: Baseline leads with a one-line 'Token bucket.' paragraph followed by bullets; the literal first paragraph contains no reason. Reword to 'pick and project-tied reason appear before any generic comparison' so the assertion is unambiguous.
No assertion checks fidelity of quotes attributed to the user. The baseline misquoted NOTES.md ('pick one and revisit'); that went uncaught by the existing assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline passes 6/7 with no skill, so most assertions here measure what the model already does on a 'too long, try again' prompt. The invented-default-numbers assertion is the only discriminator and its wording leaves the baseline's case ambiguous.
